title: Appendix A — Draft: Data Documentation
text:
Goal is to give evidence to my boss that shark-infested storms are very rare, if not impossible.
The data I found is from the NOAA data base. I extracted tornado data from Los Angeles (the setting of Sharknado), Florida (tropical storms are abundant), South Carolina (another more tropical place), and Oklahoma (the tornado capitol of the nation).
All the data sets are the same format. They were collected from the same data base NOAA.gov.
These are the important aspects of the data sets collected

County Location
Begin Location
Begin Date
Begin Time
Tornado F Scale
Direct Deaths
Direct Injuries
Property Damage
Tornado Length and Width
End Location
End Date
End Time

Measurements are take by the MWS Storm Survey, Spotters, State officials and the Public

Florida tornado data: “Storm Events Database - Search Results  National Centers for Environmental Information” (n.d.a)
South Carolina tornado data: “Storm Events Database - Search Results  National Centers for Environmental Information” (n.d.b)
Oklahoma tornado data: “Storm Events Database - Search Results  National Centers for Environmental Information” (n.d.c)
Los Angeles tornado data: “Storm Events Database - Search Results  National Centers for Environmental Information” (n.d.d)
